tests.title: Agent mode suppresses banner and spinner and emits one JSON object
given: a spec root with two specs exists
then: stdout parses as exactly one JSON object
stdout contains no banner or spinner characters
tests.pseudocode: r = run(env={AF_AGENT:'1'}, 'spec list'); assert parse_json(r.stdout).ok == true; assert not contains(r.stdout, BANNER_TEXT)

tests.title: AF_AGENT=1 combined with --quiet behaves like AF_AGENT=1 alone
given: a spec root with two specs exists
tests.when: spec list and spec --quiet list are executed
then: stdout, stderr and exit code are identical for both invocations
tests.pseudocode: a = run(env, 'spec list'); b = run(env, 'spec --quiet list'); assert a == b

tests.title: For any command, agent mode never writes non-JSON to stdout
tests.when: for any command in {list, status, validate, render, lint} with minimal valid arguments
then: every diagnostic line appears on stderr only
tests.pseudocode: for cmd in COMMANDS: r = run(env, cmd); assert is_json(r.stdout)

tests.title: Command error in agent mode is reported as a JSON envelope on stdout
then: stdout parses as JSON with ok == false and a non-empty error string
tests.pseudocode: r = run(env, 'spec status 99_missing'); assert r.code == 1; j = parse_json(r.stdout); assert j.ok == false and len(j.error) > 0

tests.title: Closed stdout pipe does not change the exit code
given: stdout is connected to a reader that closes before the payload is written
then: no panic trace appears on stderr
tests.pseudocode: r = run_with_closed_stdout(env, 'spec list'); assert r.code == 0; assert not contains(r.stderr, 'panic')

tests.title: An agent lists specs end to end through the compiled binary
given: a spec root with one spec exists
tests.when: AF_AGENT=1 spec list is executed against the real binary
then: stdout is one JSON object whose specs array has one entry
